research_mode: official Home Office sources only; police-recorded-crime open-data schema, outcome data-flow, technical definitions and special-collection linkage gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Police recorded crime financial-year field
verified_claims: Financial Year combined with Financial Quarter identifies when offences were initially recorded
each financial year runs from April to March
limitations: the field is a recording/reporting period and not an exact incident timestamp

sources.name: Police recorded crime quarter mapping
verified_claims: Quarter 1 is April to June, Quarter 2 July to September, Quarter 3 October to December, and Quarter 4 January to March
limitations: quarter labels must be interpreted within the stated financial year

sources.name: Police-force-area geography field
verified_claims: Force Name identifies the police force area in which the offence was recorded
this will generally be the same area where the offence took place
limitations: generally does not guarantee an exact occurrence location or parcel

sources.name: Community Safety Partnership geography field
verified_claims: CSP Name identifies the Community Safety Partnership area in which offences were recorded
a CSP generally corresponds to single or combined local-authority boundaries
limitations: CSP geography is not a parcel boundary

sources.name: Police recorded crime offence hierarchy
verified_claims: Offence codes map to offence descriptions, subgroups and groups
limitations: classification hierarchy must not be treated as independent additive categories without code-level checks

sources.name: Police recorded crime count-cell semantics
verified_claims: each row contains a count for a specified offence code, area, financial year and financial quarter
limitations: a row is an aggregate count and not an individual crime record

sources.name: Centrally recorded fraud rows
verified_claims: PFA tables include quarterly centrally recorded fraud data from Action Fraud, Cifas and Financial Fraud UK from 2011/12
the relevant rows are identified through force, subgroup and offence-code fields
limitations: central fraud rows are not territorial-force parcel observations

sources.name: Police recorded crime geographic reference table
verified_claims: the geographic reference table maps CSP values to police force areas, regions and ONS codes
limitations: the ONS code identifies the CSP and does not identify a property

sources.name: Police recorded crime offence reference versions
verified_claims: the offence reference table provides old pre-July-2013 and new post-July-2013 offence groups and subgroups
limitations: time-series joins must retain the applicable classification version

sources.name: Police recorded crime quarter additivity
verified_claims: figures in the PRC tables are additive
four quarters can be summed for a 12-month PFA total
limitations: addition is valid only after matching area, offence and period dimensions

sources.name: CSP-level British Transport Police exclusion
verified_claims: British Transport Police data are excluded from CSP-level police recorded crime data
CSP totals therefore need not equal national totals
limitations: CSP data must not be presented as complete national coverage

sources.name: Making-off-without-payment back series
verified_claims: offence code 49A was introduced separately in April 2013
the 2002/03 to 2012/13 back series mixes actual force data and estimated data
limitations: the reconstructed back series is not uniformly observed

sources.name: Burglary classification from April 2017
verified_claims: residential and non-residential burglary replaced domestic and non-domestic burglary from April 2017
limitations: the classification change requires a time-series break or mapping

sources.name: Residential burglary split from April 2023
verified_claims: residential burglary was split into residential home and residential unconnected buildings from April 2023
limitations: the newer subcategories should not be silently backfilled

sources.name: Police recorded crime rate convention
verified_claims: low-volume crime rates are typically calculated per 1,000 population using ONS population estimates
limitations: rate denominators must match the geographic and temporal scope
